content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

It defines:

- Saving, viewing, editing, and deleting bookmarks
- Search, tags, filtering, and sorting
- Validation, duplicate handling, persistence, and accessibility
- A private, single-user first release
- Clear exclusions such as sharing, imports, browser extensions, and automatic metadata retrieval

The quality checklist passed all 16 checks: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md).

No code or implementation plan has been created yet. Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll move to `speckit-plan`.

Thanks for putting this together — I read through it, and a lot of it matches what I picture: saving links, editing them, tags, search, filtering, sorting, and having everything still there when I come back. That part feels right.

But a few things in here — especially some of what you've marked as *not* included — aren't what I had in mind, so I'd like some changes before we move on.

The big one: **when I save a link, I really don't want to type in the title and everything myself.** I'd expect that if I just paste a web address, the app goes and grabs the page's title, its description, and its little icon for me, and fills those in — and then I can tweak them if I want. You've listed "automatically retrieving page titles, descriptions, favicons" as something left out, and that's honestly one of the main reasons I'd use a tool like this instead of just a plain list. Please bring that in.

A few more things I expected that I don't see:

- **A "read later" idea.** When I save something I haven't gotten to yet, I'd like to mark it as unread and be able to look at just my unread pile, then mark things read as I get through them.
- **Tucking links away without deleting them.** Sometimes I'm done with a link but don't want to throw it out forever. I'd want to move it out of my main list into a separate "archived" area I can still go back to — different from deleting, which should be permanent.
- **Smarter searching.** Beyond plain text matching, I'd expect to search by a tag directly, put a phrase in quotes for an exact match, and combine terms (this one *and* that, or *not* that).
- **Handling a lot at once.** If I select several links, I'd like to do one action to all of them — like tagging them or archiving them together.
- **Getting my existing bookmarks in, and my collection back out.** I've got bookmarks elsewhere, so being able to bring them in from a standard bookmarks file, and export mine the same way, matters to me. I saw import/export listed as excluded — I'd want those.

The re-saving behavior you described is exactly right — if I try to save something I already saved, point me at the one I've got rather than making a duplicate. And keeping it private and single-user for now is fine with me.

Could you revise the spec to cover these? Once it reflects the above I'll be glad to look again.

content:
The revised specification is ready: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md).

It now includes:

- Automatic title, description, and favicon retrieval with editable suggestions and graceful failure
- Unread/read status, with new bookmarks defaulting to unread
- Archiving and restoration, separate from permanent deletion
- Exact phrases, `tag:` criteria, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` search
- Bulk tagging, status changes, archiving, restoration, and deletion
- Standard browser bookmark HTML import/export
- Folder-to-tag conversion during import
- Full-state round trips when re-importing the app’s own exports

The revised spec contains six user journeys, 47 functional requirements, and ten measurable outcomes. All 16 quality checks pass in [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md).

No planning or implementation has started. Please approve this revision or identify any further changes; approval unlocks the `speckit-plan` stage.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I was worried about, and reading through it I can really picture using it.

Walking through it in my head: I paste a link and it fills in the title, description, and icon for me, and I can fix any of those; my other typing isn't lost if something goes wrong; a link I've already saved sends me to the one I've got instead of doubling up; new things start as unread and I can look at just my unread pile; I can tuck links into an archive and pull them back without losing anything, separate from deleting for good; I can search by a tag, quote an exact phrase, and combine terms; I can select a bunch and tag, archive, or clear them in one go; and I can bring my existing bookmarks in from a browser file — with the folders becoming tags, which I like — and get everything back out again. That all matches what I wanted.

One small thing I noticed while reading, more of a question than a complaint: I can write a personal note on a bookmark, which is good — when I look at that note later, will it show up nicely formatted if I use simple things like a bit of bold or a bulleted list? I don't need anything fancy, I just want my notes to be readable rather than showing raw symbols.

And one idea for down the road, not something to hold this up: since I can now build fairly specific searches, it'd be handy someday to save a search I use a lot so I can jump back to it without retyping. That can wait — no need to add it now.

Other than the note-formatting question, I'm happy with this specification. If notes display readably, go ahead and approve it as far as I'm concerned, and move on to planning.

Notes will display as formatted content—paragraphs, bold, italic, lists, and safe links—rather than raw symbols. Saved searches remain a future enhancement.

The implementation plan is ready for review:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [Validation guide](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Search grammar](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/search-query.ebnf)
- [Bookmark HTML contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/bookmark-html.md)

The plan uses a React/Node application with SQLite, hardened server-side metadata retrieval, locally stored icons, safe CommonMark rendering, structured search parsing, and portable browser bookmark HTML.

All plan checks pass, the API contract validates, and no clarifications remain. No tasks or application code have been created. Please approve the plan or request changes; approval unlocks `speckit-tasks`.

That all sounds good — thank you for confirming the notes will show up properly formatted with bold, lists, and the like. That's exactly what I wanted, and I'm fine with saved searches being a later addition.

I'll be honest that the technical details of the plan are mostly over my head — the pieces about how it's built aren't really something I can judge. What matters to me is that it delivers everything we agreed on in the spec: the automatic title-and-icon fetching when I paste a link, the read-later and archive workflows, the tag and phrase and combined searching, doing things to many bookmarks at once, bringing bookmarks in and out with folders becoming tags, my notes showing nicely formatted, and everything staying put and private between visits. As long as the plan holds all of that, I'm happy for you to go ahead.

Go ahead and move on to the next step.

content:
The bookmark manager is built, verified, and running at:

**http://maker:4000**

Review password: `review-bookmarks`

It includes automatic page metadata and icon retrieval, formatted notes, advanced search, read-later and archive workflows, bulk actions, duplicate prevention, persistent private storage, and browser HTML import/export with folder-to-tag conversion.

Validation passed:

- 23 unit, integration, security, and contract tests
- 4 performance gates, including 10,000-bookmark import/search
- 3 desktop/mobile Chromium and accessibility journeys
- Clean production build and dependency audit

Setup and operational details are in [README.md](/work/README.md), with full results in [verification.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/verification.md).

I spent some real time poking at the live app, and it does what we agreed on. Here's what I saw for myself:

- I pasted a link and saved it, gave it tags, and it came back with everything in place.
- When I tried to save the very same link again, it stopped me and pointed me right at the one I already had — exactly the no-duplicates behavior I wanted.
- Searching works the way I hoped: I found things by a tag, put a phrase in quotes and got only the exact match, and combined terms with "and"/"or" to narrow things down. Capitalization didn't trip it up either.
- My unread pile behaves properly — a link shows up there until I mark it read, then it drops out, and comes back if I mark it unread again.
- Archiving tucks a link out of my main list into a separate archive I can still get to, and it's kept apart from deleting for good.
- I could add a note with bold text and a bulleted list, and it's stored as my formatted note.
- And it's behind a password, so it's private like we said.

Between that and your verification report covering the bulk actions, the import/export round-trip with folders becoming tags, the formatted-note display, and everything surviving repeated reopens, I'm satisfied this is the app I asked for.

The one thing we set aside — being able to save a search I use often — I'm still keen on eventually, but as we agreed that's for a later round and it's not holding anything up now.

This is what I wanted. I'm happy to accept it.
